title: What Is Audiobook Studio
desc: A local-first app that turns manuscripts into finished audiobooks with AI voice cloning — a full production surface, not one-click text-to-speech.
lede: Audiobook Studio is a local-first app that turns a manuscript into a finished, multi-voice audiobook using AI voice cloning — all on your own machine.
body:
At a glance
  • It runs on your computer; your text and audio stay local unless you choose otherwise.
  • It's a production surface, not one-click text-to-speech — you direct narration line by line.
  • One default local engine means no accounts and no per-word cost.
  • You assemble narrated chapters into a real audiobook file (M4B/MP3).

A production tool, not a "read it aloud" button

Most text-to-speech tools give you one voice and one pass. Audiobook Studio is built for the messy reality of a whole book: many characters, lines that need a second take, pronunciation you want to fix, and a finished file at the end.

You stay in control of the result. Assign a voice to the narrator and a different one to each character, regenerate just the lines you change, and listen back as you go.

What it does

  • Multi-voice narration. Give the narrator one voice and every character their own.
  • Voice cloning & a library. Build voices from samples; organize them with icons and tags.
  • Targeted repair. Edit a line and regenerate only that segment — no charge.
  • Assembly & export. Combine finished chapters into an audiobook file.

Local-first by design

Your manuscript, samples, and audio stay on your machine. The default voice engine runs locally, so you can narrate an entire book with no account and no usage meter. If you ever enable an optional cloud engine, that choice is explicit and clearly disclosed.

Tip — Prefer to keep everything offline? You can. The local engine needs no network once it's set up.

How the pieces fit together

  1. Project & chapters — your book, broken into chapters of text.
  2. Voices & casting — voices assigned to the narrator and characters.
  3. Generation — a managed engine turns assigned text into audio.
  4. Assembly — finished chapters become a single audiobook file.

In 2.0, generation runs in a managed, crash-isolated TTS Server with installable engines. See Studio 2.0 at a Glance.
